narrative.overview: Skillist is an instrument panel for production agent behavior. It looks the way a well-built piece of engineering hardware looks: monochrome, squared, precisely ruled, nothing on the surface that isn't a control or a readout. The people using it are staking production agents on the skills catalogued here, so the interface earns trust the way an instrument does, by being legible, honest about state, and free of decoration that could be mistaken for meaning. The system is deliberately quiet. Hierarchy comes from scale, weight, and space, not from color or heavy borders. Chrome is treated as a cost: surfaces are flat with a single hairline ring, depth is implied rather than dramatized, and the one chromatic voice on screen (destructive red) means exactly one thing.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome by default; grayscale ink ramp carries the entire UI.
Squared geometry everywhere (0px radius on controls, cards, and images).
Uppercase, wide-tracked micro-labels on buttons and badges.
Hairline rings instead of shadows; flat at rest.
One reserved signal accent, held out of active use until deliberately introduced.

rules.name: The One Chromatic Voice Rule
rules.body: In normal operation, destructive red is the only saturated color on screen. Everything else is grayscale. If a second hue appears and it isn't the deliberately-introduced reserved signal, it is a bug (see the stray dark-sidebar purple, oklch(0.488 0.243 264.376), a leftover to be removed).

rules.name: The Literal White Rule
rules.body: Light surface is exactly oklch(1 0 0). Never warm-tint the background toward cream, sand, or paper. Warmth, if it ever arrives, lives in the reserved accent, never in the canvas.

rules.name: The Equipment-Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase + wide tracking is reserved for short labels (<=4 words): buttons, badges, control captions. Never set a sentence or body copy in all caps.

rules.name: The Machine-Voice Rule
rules.body: Any literal machine value (id, hash, path, JSON) is set in mono. Human prose is never mono; machine output is never proportional. The typeface tells you who is speaking.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If you reach for a shadow larger than shadow-sm, stop: the answer is a hairline, a tonal step, or nothing. Floating, lifted, and glowing cards are prohibited.

dos: Do keep geometry squared: 0px radius on buttons, badges, cards, and images.
Do build hierarchy from scale, weight, and space (400 -> 600 -> 700), then a hairline, then tonal layering. Reach for color last.
Do set every machine value in mono, and every short control label in uppercase tracked micro-type.
Do hold the surface at literal white oklch(1 0 0) in light mode and near-black oklch(0.145 0 0) in dark; both themes must pass 4.5:1 for body text.
Do keep the reserved signal amber out of active use until introduced deliberately, and cap it at <=10% of any screen.
Do pair every status with a word or shape, and give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
donts: Don't ship the generic shadcn / AI-default look: no soft rounded cards, no decorative purple accent, no gray-on-tinted body text.
Don't drift playful / consumer / rounded: no bubbly radii, no emoji-forward UI, no illustration where a control belongs.
Don't become a cluttered enterprise dashboard: no heavy borders, no gray-on-gray tables without hierarchy, no density for its own sake.
Don't dress up like loud SaaS marketing: no gradient heroes, no gradient-clip text headings, no glassmorphism, no hero-metric template.
Don't use a shadow larger than shadow-sm, a colored background chip for a badge, or a boxed input.
Don't encode status in color alone, set body copy in all caps, or introduce a second typeface.
